settings.question: Do pickleball paddles need stringing?

settings.answer: It depends on your hand, your budget, and how you play, and the honest way to find out is to hit with one. I keep demo paddles for that. Try one for a few days, and if you like it, I order yours. If you already know the model you want, I can order that one for you.
settings.question: Which paddle should I buy?

settings.answer: Overgrip replacement is $5. A replacement grip is $20. Building a grip up to a larger size is $25. Those are the same prices as my tennis racquet grip work.
settings.question: What does grip work cost?

settings.answer: No. Everything is local pickup by appointment in the Kansas City Northland. It keeps the cost down and lets you see the paddle before you pay for it.
settings.question: Do you ship?

settings.answer: Yes. I stock outdoor and indoor balls, overgrips, edge guard tape, and lead tape, and I can order anything else my supplier carries.

settings.title: Demo Paddle Program
settings.subtitle: Borrow a demo paddle at a Kansas City Northland meetup. Keep it up to a week. No cost, no obligation.
settings.intro_content:
Why demo a paddle before you buy? Because the spec sheets all sound the same, and the difference between a power paddle and a control paddle is something you feel in your hand, not something you read. Price does not settle it either. A $150 paddle you like beats a $280 paddle you fight.

The program works like my tennis demo program: borrow a paddle at a Northland meetup, take it to your court for up to a week, and decide with real games behind you. No sales pitch. If you like it, I order yours. If you don't, bring it back.
settings.items_desc: Five paddles that cover the questions players actually ask: power or control, premium or mid-priced, and what $100 gets you.

settings.title: Pick Your Paddles
settings.description: Look through the fleet below and pick one, or two, that you want to try. Power against control is the comparison most players need to make.

settings.title: Book a Demo Meetup
settings.description: Pick a time online and I will bring the paddles to the QuikTrip at 9600 N Oak Trafficway. Then call or text me at 816-938-7622 and tell me which paddles you picked.

settings.title: Hit With It for a Week
settings.description: Take the paddle to your court and play real games with it for up to a week. It is free, and I do not take a credit card. You sign a short demo agreement at pickup.

settings.title: Decide on Your Terms
settings.description: Love it? I order yours, and I set the grip up before you pick it up. Not for you? Just bring it back. No pressure.

settings.name: Perseus Pro IV 16mm
settings.tagline: The paddle players ask for by name. A power-leaning all-court paddle with a raw carbon face.
settings.best_for: Intermediate to advanced players who hit with power and want the paddle they see on tour.

settings.name: LUXX Control Air Invikta
settings.tagline: Selkirk's control flagship in the elongated Invikta shape. Built for resets, blocks, and touch at the net.
settings.best_for: Control players, and tennis players crossing over who place the ball first and hit through it second.

settings.name: Double Black Diamond Control 16mm
settings.tagline: The mid-priced benchmark. Raw carbon face, heavy spin, and controlled power. Shown in the blue colorway.
settings.best_for: Most players. If you only demo one paddle, this is the one the others have to beat.

settings.name: SLK Halo Power
settings.tagline: The step down that still feels like a real paddle. A thinner 13 mm core puts more pop off the face.
settings.best_for: Casual players becoming regulars, and anyone who wants power without the premium price.

settings.name: SLK Evo Control 2.0 Max
settings.tagline: The starter paddle that is not a toy. A wide Max face and a thick control core at a beginner price.
settings.best_for: New players, and a second paddle for the family bag.

settings.question: What does it cost?
settings.answer: Nothing. The demo is completely free, and I don't take a credit card for it. I just ask you to sign a short demo agreement at pickup.

settings.question: Do I need to sign anything?
settings.answer: Yes. A short demo agreement and liability waiver at pickup. It covers the return timeline, responsibility for damage or loss, and a standard liability release. Takes about two minutes.

settings.question: How long can I keep it?
settings.answer: Up to one week. Long enough to play real games on your own court, not just swing it in a store.

settings.question: How many paddles can I take?
settings.answer: One or two at a time, so you can compare a power paddle against a control paddle in the same session.

settings.question: Where do I pick up and return?
settings.answer: The QuikTrip at 9600 N Oak Trafficway in Kansas City, or another Northland spot we arrange. Same meetup as my stringing service.

settings.question: What if the paddle I want is not in the fleet?
settings.answer: Tell me the model. If my racquet sports supplier carries it, I will order it for you, and you pay when you pick it up. How ordering works is covered in the next section.
